title: Changes of State
seo_title: Primary 5 Basic Science and Technology: Changes of State Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 5 Basic Science and Technology: Living and Non-Living Things
standard_text: Matter changes state when heat is added or removed: melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation, boiling and sublimation. The particles move faster when heated. Diagrams and flowcharts show changes of state. (summary of the Basic Science and Technology curriculum, Primary 5, theme: Living and Non-Living Things)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 Basic Science and Technology worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Living and Non-Living Things): solids, liquids and gases, melting and freezing, evaporation and condensation, and the particle model. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Melting, evaporation and boiling need heat.
body_html:
How to think about it

Matter can change from one state to another. Heating a solid can melt it into a liquid; heating a liquid can make it evaporate or boil into a gas. Cooling a gas makes it condense into a liquid; cooling a liquid makes it freeze.

When matter is heated, its particles move faster and farther apart. During melting or boiling, the temperature stays the same until the change is complete. Changes of state are physical changes because no new substance forms.

Example

Ice cream melts in the sun. Which change of state?

Solid to liquid

Answer: melting

Example

Water droplets form on a cold glass. Which change?

Gas to liquid

Answer: condensation

Common mistakes

  • Thinking boiling and evaporation are the same.
  • Thinking condensation comes from inside the glass.
  • Thinking a change of state makes a new substance.
